Person.comment:
Ron Caspi received his PhD in Marine Microbiology in 1996 from the Scripps Institution of Oceanography in La Jolla, CA, under the guidance of Dr. Bradley Tebo and Dr. Margo Haygood. He completed his post-graduate education in 1999 with Dr. Donald Helinski at the Center for Molecular Genetics at UC San Diego.

After three years with Pangene Corporation, where he managed the automation and bioinformatics department, Ron joined SRI International in 2004, and has been the head curator of the MetaCyc database ever since.

Protein.comment:
The eutG gene of Salmonella enterica is located in the ethanolamine utilization operon, and encodes a 391-amino-acid protein with a strong similarity to several characterized alcohol dehydrogenases. Sequence analysis also suggested that the enzyme binds iron and uses an NAD coenzyme.

A ΔeutG strain grew at pH 7 or below, but not at pH 8, and released more acetaldehyde than wild-type cells during growth on glycerol and ethanolamine. The mutant was not able to grow with ethanolamine as the sole carbon source [Penrod06].

The phenotype was corrected by providing a different carbon source, suggesting that EutG helps to conserve or use acetaldehyde rather than removing a toxic accumulation. The authors speculated that EutG may simply serve to help recycle electron carriers and balance redox reactions during fermentation, by converting excess acetaldehyde to ethanol and NADH to NAD [Penrod06].
